Question Choices: Four fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that at least one result is even?
Hints: Use the complement that all four results are odd;Each die is odd with probability 1/2;Subtract (1/2)^4 from 1
Solution: The probability that all four dice are odd is $(1/2)^4=1/16$.;Therefore the probability of at least one even result is $1-1/16=15/16$.

Question Choices: Two cards are drawn from a standard deck without replacement. What is the probability that at least one card is a heart?
Hints: Use the complement that neither card is a heart;There are 39 non-hearts at first and 38 after one is drawn;Subtract (39/52)(38/51) from 1
Solution: The probability of two non-hearts is $(39/52)(38/51)=19/34$.;Thus the probability of at least one heart is $1-19/34=15/34$.

Question Choices: A four-character digit code uses digits 0 through 9, with repetition allowed. What is the probability that the code contains at least one 7?
Hints: Use the complement that no position contains 7;Each position has 9 allowed digits in the complement;Subtract (9/10)^4 from 1
Solution: The probability that no position is $7$ is $(9/10)^4=6561/10000$.;Therefore the probability of at least one $7$ is $1-6561/10000=3439/10000$.

Question Choices: A bag contains 6 white and 4 black marbles. Four marbles are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that at least one is black?
Hints: Use the complement that all four marbles are white;Compare C(6,4) with C(10,4);Subtract from 1
Solution: The all-white probability is $C(6,4)/C(10,4)=15/210=1/14$.;Thus the probability of at least one black marble is $1-1/14=13/14$.
